articles.title: Meet Sir Darius Brown, the 19-year-old who has made 7,000 bow ties for shelter pets and helped raise more than $500,000 to help animals find homes
articles.summary: US News: When Sir Darius Brown was in elementary school, he struggled with reading and speech challenges that made him feel different from his classmates. He f.
articles.body: When Sir Darius Brown was in elementary school, he struggled with reading and speech challenges that made him feel different from his classmates. He found comfort in animals, and in bow ties. That combination sparked a mission: to help shelter pets get adopted by dressing them in handmade bow ties that make them stand out in photos and at adoption events. Now 19, Brown has created around 7,000 bow ties for dogs and cats in shelters across the U.S. and beyond, and his nonprofit has helped raise more than $500,000 to support animal rescue and adoption efforts. His story, as told to Woman’s World, is a reminder that a small, creative idea can grow into a nationwide movement for good.A childhood challenge turned into purposeSir Darius Brown grew up in New Jersey, where he was diagnosed with learning and speech difficulties, including dyslexia and a speech disorder. In school, he was sometimes teased and struggled to fit in. At the same time, he had a deep love for animals, especially dogs and cats, and spent as much time as he could with pets at home and in his community.Bow ties became a signature part of his style. He liked how they made him feel confident and polished, and he noticed that people responded positively when he wore them. Over time, he began to wonder: if bow ties made him feel special, could they do the same for shelter animals?The birth of Beaux & PawsIn 2016, when he was just 10 years old, Brown launched Beaux & Paws, a nonprofit dedicated to helping shelter pets get adopted. The concept was simple but powerful: make colourful, photogenic bow ties for dogs and cats, donate them to shelters, and use the images to draw attention to animals who might otherwise be overlooked.He started by making bow ties at home with help from his mother, Syrita Brown, who taught him how to sew and supported his vision. Early batches were small, but as photos of bow-tied shelter pets began circulating on social media, interest grew. Shelters reported that animals wearing bow ties often got more likes, more shares and more adoption inquiries.7,000 bow ties and countingSince launching Beaux & Paws, Brown estimates that he and his volunteers have made and donated around 7,000 bow ties to shelters, rescue groups and individual animals in need. The bow ties come in all colours and patterns, from bright solids to holiday themes, and are designed to fit both dogs and cats of various sizes.Each bow tie is more than an accessory; it’s a tool for storytelling. When a shelter posts a photo of a dog or cat wearing a Beaux & Paws bow tie, the image tends to stand out in a feed full of adoption posts. That extra attention can be the difference between an animal lingering in a kennel for months and finding a home in days.More than accessories: fundraising and advocacyBeaux & Paws does not stop at bow ties. The organisation also raises money to support shelters and rescue groups, helping cover costs such as: veterinary care, including vaccinations, spay/neuter surgeries and treatment for injuries or illness; food, bedding and other daily necessities for animals waiting for homes; and adoption events and marketing efforts to connect pets with potential families.To date, Brown says Beaux & Paws has helped raise more than $500,000 for animal welfare causes. Funds come from donations, merchandise sales, partnerships with businesses and community events where bow ties are sold or auctioned.A national (and international) impactWhat began as a local New Jersey project has grown into a nationwide effort. Beaux & Paws has donated bow ties and support to shelters in dozens of states, from large municipal facilities to small, volunteer-run rescues. The organisation has also sent bow ties to animal welfare groups in other countries, extending its reach beyond the U.S.Shelter staff and volunteers often share stories of specific animals whose adoption prospects improved after they were photographed in bow ties. In some cases, dogs and cats that had been in the system for months were adopted within days of new photos being posted. While it is impossible to attribute every adoption to a bow tie, Brown and his partners believe the visual boost plays a meaningful role.Balancing school, life and a growing nonprofitAs Beaux & Paws grew, Brown had to balance his mission with school, friendships and typical teenage life. He has spoken openly about continuing to work on his reading and speech challenges while running a nonprofit, travelling for events and managing donations and partnerships.His mother has been a constant support, helping with logistics, sewing and communications, especially in the early years. Over time, a network of volunteers, many of them young people, has joined the effort, making bow ties, organising drives and spreading the word on social media.Recognition and inspirationBrown’s work has drawn attention from media outlets, animal welfare organisations and community groups. He has been featured in news stories, invited to speak at schools and honoured by animal rescue groups for his contributions. But for him, the most important recognition comes from the animals themselves, or rather, from the families who adopt them.He often receives photos and messages from adopters showing their newly named “Sir” or “Lady” something, dressed in a bow tie at home, on a couch or in a yard. Those updates, he says, are the real reward.Why bow ties workThere is a simple psychology behind the bow tie effect. Shelter environments can be stressful, and photos taken in kennels do not always show an animal’s personality. A bright bow tie adds colour, charm and a sense of occasion, making the animal look cared for and special.For potential adopters scrolling through dozens of posts, a bow-tied pet can feel like a story waiting to happen: a dog ready for weddings and family photos, a cat destined for sunny windowsills and lap time. That emotional connection can be enough to prompt a visit, an application and, ultimately, an adoption.Looking aheadNow 19, Brown sees Beaux & Paws as a long-term mission, not just a childhood project. He hopes to continue expanding the programme, reaching more shelters and raising more funds to help animals find homes. He also wants to keep encouraging other young people to find their own ways to make a difference, whether through animals, the environment or their communities.For Sir Darius Brown, the bow tie was first a way to feel confident in a world that sometimes felt hard to navigate. Today, it is a symbol of hope for thousands of shelter pets, and proof that one person’s small idea, pursued with persistence, can change many lives.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: MP highway crash: 5 killed, 20 hurt after bus collides with bulker; PM Modi mourns deaths
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: At least five people were killed and around 20 injured after a passenger bus collided with a bulker truck, on National Highway 39 near Badw.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: At least five people were killed and around 20 injured after a passenger bus collided with a bulker truck, on National Highway 39 near Badwar stand in Madhya Pradesh’s Rewa district on Wednesday.The collision sent the bus off the road and into a roadside ditch, district collector and district magistrate Narendra Kumar Suryavanshi told news agency ANI.“The collision between the bus and the other vehicle, a ‘capsule’ [tanker], occurred at a spot about 4 kilometres ahead of Gurh. In this incident, the bus fell into a roadside ditch. Immediately, the Superintendent of Police (SP), the entire administration, medical teams, local villagers, and public representatives reached the site. Everyone here worked with sensitivity during the rescue operation,” Suryavanshi told ANI.Prime Minister Narendra Modi expressed grief over the accident and offered condolences to the families of those killed.“The loss of lives due to a mishap in Rewa, Madhya Pradesh is saddening. My thoughts are with those who have lost their loved ones. Praying for the swift recovery of the injured: PM,” the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) India said in a post on X.Giving a preliminary account of the casualties, the district magistrate said, “The rough estimate is that 20 people are injured and five have died. Everyone is engaged in the rescue operation.”The injured were being attended to as rescue operations continued at the crash site. Police and district administration officials were overseeing the response, with medical teams and local residents assisting in the rescue effort.Vice president CP Radhakrishnan also expressed condolences, saying, “Deeply saddened by the loss of precious lives in the tragic road accident in Rewa, Madhya Pradesh.“My heartfelt condolences to the bereaved families and pray for strength and solace to them in this hour of grief. I also pray for the speedy recovery of those injured in the accident.”Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Submarine en route to Israel from Germany
articles.summary: The Israeli Navy is set to add another German-built submarine to its fleet in a few days' time. The INS Drakon, built by the German company TKMS, left the Ki...
articles.body:
The Israeli Navy is adding a German-built submarine, INS Drakon, to its fleet, marking the completion of a project involving six submarines of this type for Israel.

The handover of the submarine coincides with the first test of the Israeli Lora missile by the German Navy, highlighting the close strategic cooperation and partnership between the two countries.

The delivery of German submarines to Israel is a significant aspect of German-Israeli defence cooperation, although it has faced criticism due to concerns about potential nuclear weapon retrofitting and Israeli military actions in the Gaza Strip.

The Israeli Navy is set to add another German-built submarine to its fleet in a few days' time.

The INS Drakon, built by the German company TKMS, left the Kiel shipyard on Tuesday, passed through the Kiel Canal and is now en route to Israel, according to the manufacturer.

It is the last of six submarines of this type built for Israel. It is 68 metres long and equipped with ten torpedo tubes.

Israeli Ambassador Ron Prosor pointed out that the handover is taking place at the same time as the first test of the Israeli Lora missile by the German Navy.

"This is no coincidence, but the result of close strategic cooperation and a partnership that has grown over the years," he told dpa. "We stand shoulder to shoulder as equal partners and tackle the challenges that affect us both together."

A German Navy frigate had previously successfully completed a test in the North Atlantic - kept secret until the very last moment - of the Israeli Lora missile system, which has a range of more than 500 kilometres. Plans to procure the weapons are now set to move forward.

The delivery of German submarines to Israel is a key project in German-Israeli defence cooperation and has been under way for many years.

However, the export is also controversial because, according to experts, the submarines could be retrofitted with nuclear weapons. Furthermore, German arms exports to Israel are generally subject to criticism due to the Israeli army's actions in the Gaza Strip.

The Israeli military said the submarine was on its way to the northern Israeli coastal city of Haifa. Prosor was joined by the German Naval Inspector, Jan Christian Kaack, at a farewell ceremony in Kiel.

articles.title: EU and Nato vow to step up pressure on Russia after 'new escalation' in Germany
articles.summary: Russia is accused of growing increasingly reckless after Berlin blamed Russia for a failed drone attack on Leipzig airport.
articles.body:
The heads of Nato and the European Commission have warned that Russia is growing increasingly reckless and vowed to respond to a "new normal".

"Leipzig marks a new escalation on European Union soil directly attributed to Russia," said Commission President Ursula von der Leyen, a day after Germany blamed Russia for a failed drone attack last month on Leipzig airport.

"We have to step up and that means being ready to respond to Russia's recklessness faster and better," von der Leyen said. Nato Secretary General Mark Rutte said the whole alliance, which includes the US, stood "in full solidarity with Germany".

Russia has rejected German accusations that a drone carrying explosives deliberately targeted a Ukrainian cargo plane on 4 August.

The drone was defused by a robot at Leipzig/Halle airport and a second drone is thought to have collided with another cargo plane.

A third drone was reportedly found 10 days later at the airport, which is an important Nato hub and is regularly used by Ukrainian Antonov transport aircraft.

It was not until Tuesday that the German government said police investigations and intelligence finding had proved that Russia was behind the incidents.

The interior minister said that the drone's configuration, components, explosives and detonator were all known from other Russian hybrid operations.

Two suspects have reportedly been identified in the Leipzig attack, including a Belarusian with a Russian passport who entered on a tourist visa, and another with Latvian and Russian passports who arrived by plane in Berlin and flew out two days before the failed attack.

Berlin has said it will close the Russian consulate in Bonn as well as the Russian House cultural institution, widely suspected in Berlin of acting as a propaganda outlet for the Kremlin.

The Russian foreign ministry promised to respond in "mirror-image" fashion and said Berlin had offered no evidence to back its claims. Germany's chargé d'affaires Bernd Finke was summoned to hear Moscow's rejection of Berlin's "entirely unfounded accusations".

Vladimir Putin has condemned Germany's measures as a serious mistake that "clearly runs counter to the interests of the German people".

Asked whether Moscow would be prepared to sever relations with Berlin, Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Alexander Grushko answered "maybe", but said for now it was giving diplomacy a chance.

Critics in Germany suggested the German response was relatively weak, but Berlin has its eye on a more co-ordinated response with its allies, including extended EU sanctions and entry restrictions on Russian visitors across the bloc.

Von der Leyen was clear in her statement that the Leipzig attack had involved "military-grade material carried out by Russian operatives on European Union soil".

While she was meeting Rutte in Brussels, EU foreign ministers had gathered at Wicklow in Ireland, where France's Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot said action could be taken on a European level against Russia's so-called "shadow fleet" of ships carrying oil and other cargo aimed at avoiding EU sanctions.

Barrot and fellow ministers from Belgium and the Netherlands said they had summoned Russian ambassadors in protest at the attack.

Lithuania's Foreign Minister Kestutis Budrys said it was obvious that Russia saw no political cost in its hybrid operations against European allies.

EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said they were working on how to tighten enforcement of existing sanctions, and added there was broad support for an EU visa entry ban on Russian ex-combatants as well as stricter visa limits on Russian tourists.

Several EU countries, including Sweden, the Netherlands, Poland and Spain, are pushing for more than €193bn (£165bn) in frozen Russian assets to be used to help Ukraine. The idea was first planned at the end of 2025, and rejected by Belgium where the money is held. However, Belgium's position is unchanged because it fears being held financially liable by the courts.

The Leipzig attack was part of a broader pattern of increasingly dangerous incidents, including drones and interference with critical infrastructure, von der Leyen said.

Mark Rutte added there had been increased risk to Europeans from drones and missiles crossing into countries on the Alliance's eastern flank, and there had been more "malign activities targeting our territory directly, whether it is fires set in factories producing defence equipment for Ukraine or indeed the Russian hybrid attack in Leipzig".

Several acts of suspected sabotage have been reported in Germany in the past 24 hours alone, including two attacks on electricity substations, one in the east and one in the west near Cologne.

Although authorities do not yet know who was behind the incidents, North Rhine-Westphalia Interior Minister Herbert Reul said an attack that targeted power lines at Bergheim in western Germany was deliberate and whoever had carried out was attacking the country as a whole.

"We are investigating two possibilities: sabotage directed by a foreign state and left-wing extremism," he said.

Several power lines failed prompting five power plant units to go offline at two separate coal-fired power stations. Police said six launching devices had been found in a field.

High-voltage power lines were damaged near the Jänschwalde coal-fired power plant in Brandenburg early on Tuesday and explosive devices were later found at a substation.

Meanwhile, in neighbouring Poland, Prime Minister Donald Tusk said a fire at a factory producing combat drones at Skarżysko-Kamienna, 140km (85 miles) south of Warsaw was a deliberate act of arson and sabotage. Arson has also not been ruled out in a fire at a factory in Lublin on Sunday night.

Von der Leyen said sanctions had already been used to deter Russia, and EU foreign ministers were discussing further ways of "cutting deeper in Russia's war chest".

The EU has already agreed to loan Ukraine €90bn (£77bn), and von der Leyen said Kyiv had asked for billions of extra euros in funding to help pay for PAC-3 air defence missiles. Work was already taking place on a joint Europe-Ukraine Freyja anti-ballistic missile defence project, she added.

She promised that Europe and Nato would just maintain pressure on Moscow but "we will increase it and we will not stop, not until Russia stops bombing and killing innocent children, men and children in Ukraine".

articles.title: Ukraine formally warns airlines that Russian airspace is unsafe
articles.summary: Kyiv officially notified international aviation authorities of growing risks to civilian aircraft over Russia, a day after President Zelenskyy urged foreign...
articles.body:
Ukraine has formally informed the International Civil Aviation Organisation (ICAO) that Russia's airspace is unsafe for civilian traffic, Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said on Wednesday.

"Ukraine has officially notified ICAO that the Russian airspace is not safe for civilian aviation because of increased military activity. We urge everyone to avoid it," Sybiha said on X.

He said Russia had been "deliberately ignoring the existing threats" created by its all-out war against Ukraine, arguing that the risks had already resulted in several aviation incidents in recent years.

"This is our responsible decision to notify ICAO and all airlines, and governments to take caution — even if Russia refuses to fulfill its responsibility to inform them. We want to prevent unintended incidents," Sybiha said.

The formal notification came a day after Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy warned airlines, insurers and businesses using Russian main airports that the country's airspace is now becoming increasingly dangerous as Kyiv expands its long-range drone operations.

"Today we want to warn every airline that uses Russian airspace, every insurer, everyone who still uses key Russian airports: Russian skies are becoming completely dangerous," Zelenskyy said on Tuesday.

Ukraine does not threaten civilian aviation, Zelenskyy insisted, while warning that the growing scale of Ukrainian drone operations inside Russia meant the risks could no longer be ignored.

He said Russian airspace would "effectively be closing" as the consequences of Moscow's war increasingly returned to Russian territory.

Few hours after Zelenskyy's statement, a few flights between Turkey and Moscow were disrupted overnight.

Turkish low-cost carrier Pegasus Airlines cancelled 12 flights to and from Moscow's Vnukovo Airport overnight on Wednesday, according to airport data.

A Pegasus flight from Antalya to Moscow was also diverted because of security concerns in Russian airspace, according to Turkish media reports.

Turkish Airlines, the country's flagship carrier, mostly kept its Moscow services running, although it cancelled two departures and two arrivals from and to Istanbul.

Ukraine's airspace has been closed to civilian aviation since 24 February 2022, when Russia launched its full-scale invasion.

Russian civilian aviation, by contrast, has continued operating throughout the war, despite increasingly frequent disruptions and temporary airport closures during Ukrainian drone attacks.

Despite the risks, Russian airspace still carries significant international passenger traffic.

European and US carriers stopped flying over Russia following Moscow's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.

Major airlines including Emirates, Turkish Airlines, Air India, Etihad and Qatar Airways, as well as several Chinese carriers, continue to fly to or through the country.

articles.title: In 1986, Houston bought 1,400 acres for an airport that was never built; 40 years later, the land is becoming parks and flood-control space
articles.summary: US News: Houston has finally let go of a piece of land it never knew what to do with. In 1986, the city paid $5.7 million for 1,400 acres near Brookshire on th.
articles.body: Houston has finally let go of a piece of land it never knew what to do with. In 1986, the city paid $5.7 million for 1,400 acres near Brookshire on the Katy Prairie, intending to build a third major airport to ease pressure on Bush Intercontinental and Hobby. That plan never got close to a runway. Environmentalists warned the site sat in the middle of one of the region's busiest wintering grounds for geese and waterfowl, developers and officials spent years arguing over the numbers, and the oil bust of the 1980s quietly killed off the demand the airport was meant to serve. By the late 1990s, the project was dead in all but name. Now, nearly forty years after the land was bought, Houston City Council has sold it on to Waller County for $19.7 million, not for aircraft, but for parks, wetlands and flood control.Why was Houston’s 1,400-acre airport never builtAccording to the Houston Chronicle, the Westside Airport was originally envisioned as a substantial aviation hub, with city officials and landowners planning parallel runways, advanced landing systems and hundreds of hangars, comparable in scale to Hobby Airport. However, the ambitious proposal quickly ran into resistance from Katy residents, private airport operators and environmental groups who raised concerns about the project's impact on the surrounding area.Environmental objections proved particularly significant. 1988 report by the United States Fish and Wildlife Service found that the proposed site was within one of the most active wintering areas for migratory waterfowl in the region. A consultant recorded nearly 600 geese passing over the site every hour, and federal wildlife officials estimated the airport could face as many as 50 bird strikes a month, prompting the FAA to require a full environmental impact statement before any development could proceed.Why did Houston abandon the Westside AirportAccording to the Houston Press, beyond ecological concerns, the airport plan was also driven by shifting economics. The oil downturn of the 1980s slowed corporate aviation activity and eroded the demand forecasts that had originally justified the project, according to FAA planning documents and Houston Chronicle reporting from the period.By the late 1990s, the Houston Airport System had determined that its existing facilities offered sufficient capacity for the long term, removing the practical rationale for a third airport. In the 1998 annual report, then-Mayor Lee Brown formally ended the Westside Airport proposal, recommending instead that the land be used for wetlands mitigation.Why is Houston selling the 1,400-acre propertyFor Waller County, the sale marks an unexpected turn. Duhon said the county had not anticipated that Houston would ever part with the property, noting that officials had long assumed the Houston Airport System intended to retain it. Around 600 acres of the tract are already under a conservation easement, which will continue to shape how the land can be developed, though Duhon noted the county can still pursue projects such as regional detention basins or lakes within those restrictions to help manage drainage in an area he said needs it.The land is also expected to form the basis of Waller County's first county park system, an area the county currently lacks despite anticipated population growth. Duhon said the ambition is to give residents a way to enjoy the Katy Prairie itself, through activities such as fishing, picnicking and horse riding. Houston officials have linked the sale to the city's broader financial pressures, with Duhon noting that the city is working to secure revenue for essential services, including waste collection and other municipal needs.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Iranian attack on Saudi tanker killed two sailors, Saudi Arabia says
articles.summary: The kingdom condemns the targeting of Sidr, which was reportedly hit by unknown projectiles in the Strait of Hormuz on Monday.
articles.body:
Saudi Arabia has condemned what it said was an Iranian attack on a Saudi-owned supertanker on Monday night that killed two Filipino sailors.

The Saudi national shipping company, Bahri, confirmed on Wednesday that its vessel Sidr was "involved in a security incident while transiting the Strait of Hormuz".

Sidr was hit by projectiles north of Oman's Musandam Peninsula, according to maritime security firms. A South Korean-owned supertanker, Senegal Prosperity, was reportedly struck east of Musandam around the same time.

Iran has not responded to the Saudi allegation. But it said earlier that two tankers had caught fire after hitting mines while using an unauthorised route through the strait.

The news of the sailors' deaths came after the US military carried out a wave of air strikes on Iran and Iranian forces targeted US bases in neighbouring Arab states with missiles and drones in their biggest exchange of fire since July .

On Wednesday Iran's health minister said 18 people were killed and 108 injured in the US attacks. Iran has accused the US of a "war crime" over a strike that killed four people including two children at a wedding party in the southern city of Sirik. The US military said it was looking into the reports.

Shipping company Bahri's statement said the unspecified "security incident" affecting Sidr happened in the Strait of Hormuz at around 23:40 local time (19:40 GMT) on Monday.

"It is with profound sadness that Bahri confirms the loss of two of its Filipino seafarers as a result of the incident," it added. "The company extends its deepest condolences and heartfelt sympathies to their families, loved ones, and colleagues during this difficult time."

Later, the Saudi foreign ministry expressed the kingdom's condemnation of "Iran's targeting of the Saudi tanker (Sidr) while it was transiting the Strait of Hormuz".

It also condemned the recent Iranian attacks on Jordan, Bahrain and Kuwait, and stressed the "need to halt escalation and respect the security and safety of international navigation", as well as the security of global energy supplies, national sovereignty, and international law.

The statements were issued a day after maritime risk management and intelligence firms Marisks and Kpler reported that two tankers each loaded with two million barrels of Saudi crude oil were struck by unknown projectiles within minutes of each other as they transited outbound through the Strait of Hormuz late on Monday.

Sidr was struck by "unknown projectiles" at 19:52 GMT about 16 nautical miles (30km) north-east of Khasab, Oman, while Senegal Prosperity was struck by "three unknown projectiles" about 17 nautical miles east of Khasab, according to Marisks.

The UK Maritime Trade Operations agency also reported two incidents in the same locations.

On Wednesday, Iran's Islamic Revolution Guard Corps said in a statement that two oil tankers sought "at the urging of the US military to transit via an illegal route" in the Strait of Hormuz before "striking mines and exploding". The vessels were "currently on fire", it added.

The US military has not commented, but it said the latest strikes on Iran followed "recent attempted attacks by the IRGC against commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz and against American service members".

The Strait of Hormuz, through which a fifth of global oil and gas shipments usually pass, has effectively been closed since the start of the US and Israel's war with Iran in February due to Iranian missile and drone attacks on commercial vessels and a US blockade of Iranian ports.

The US and Iran reached a preliminary agreement to end the war and reopen the strait in June, but it collapsed within weeks after the Iranian attacks on shipping resumed and the US reinstated its blockade.

Iran has insisted it will not give up some measure of control over the waterway and has targeted vessels using a southern route through Omani waters that avoids its preferred route through Iranian waters.

Despite the Iranian attacks, US President Donald Trump has declared that the strait is "open" and the US military has been helping ships navigate the southern route.

US Energy Secretary Chris Wright said 17 million barrels of oil flowed through the Strait of Hormuz by ship on Monday - a record daily total since the start of the war.

articles.title: US nurse found dead with 2 sons in suspected double murder-suicide
articles.summary: US News: A Minnesota community is mourning the deaths of a 43-year-old nurse and her two adult sons in a suspected double murder-suicide, police said.Jamie Lee.
articles.body: A Minnesota community is mourning the deaths of a 43-year-old nurse and her two adult sons in a suspected double murder-suicide, police said.Jamie Lee Charles, 43, and her sons Jaymison Samuel Shaw, 22, and William Samuel Shaw Jr., 19, were found dead Sunday at their townhouse in Inver Grove Heights during a welfare check, according to police.Preliminary findings indicate the incident was a double murder-suicide, Inver Grove Heights Police Chief Melissa Chiodo said. Investigators have identified Jaymison as the suspect, adding that the incident appeared to have been contained within the residence.Police have not disclosed how the three died or what prompted the welfare check. Police have not announced a possible motive.Charles had worked as a nurse with the Minneapolis VA Health Care System for nine years. Just days before her death, she shared a photo from the Minnesota State Fair with Fox 9 chief meteorologist Ian Leonard.On Aug. 16, she had marked the anniversary of a serious health crisis in a Facebook post, writing that a year earlier she had been “laying in a hospital dying.”“I didn’t understand how with a blink of an eye my life got flipped upside down,” she wrote, thanking her family and friends for supporting her through her recovery.Charles frequently celebrated her sons on social media. Jaymison had turned 22 in June, while William, known as Willie, graduated high school last year and played basketball for Simley High School.Family and friends gathered for a vigil Monday to remember the three. Attendees wore T-shirts bearing the words “Long live Jamie & Willie,” according to the St. Paul Pioneer Press.“There are no words that can truly express the pain of losing three precious lives,” Charles’ niece Polly Morgan said in a fundraiser, describing the three as people who brought “love, joy, and memories” to their family and community.Family members also urged people to take mental health concerns seriously in the wake of the tragedy.“Do not, absolutely do not, play with mental health,” great-aunt Ozell Shaw said, according to the Pioneer Press, urging people to seek help when someone shows warning signs.A GoFundMe has been launched to help the family with funeral and memorial expenses.Catch the latest World News and Live updates.
